acv.quote: Two hundred and fifty K ACV.

header.reason: Halima, the COO, picked the rival because it showed named people on call for on-sales. Our tiered support plans felt like 'a queue with a faster timer.' Jordan blames nothing but believes our platform was better.

findings.label: What started it
findings.finding: Aim our message at the moment payments fail mid on-sale.
findings.why: Payments failed four minutes into a Friday on-sale, and the old provider only replied after it ended.
findings.quote: They got a reply after the on-sale was over.

findings.label: Who decided
findings.finding: Show the COO who picks up, not just how the tech performs.
findings.why: Halima made the call alone in one meeting, and Ben, who wanted us, lost.
findings.quote: it was Halima's call and she made it in one meeting.

findings.label: The competitor
findings.finding: Bring the real account team, by name, into the early meetings.
findings.why: Ben said the rival brought its own engineer and account lead. Jordan's 'over-promised' doubt is only his guess.
findings.quote: A named solutions engineer and an account lead, in the room.

findings.label: Our message
findings.finding: Replace the support tiers pitch with named people for on-sales.
findings.why: Halima asked 'who's my person' and Jordan walked her through tiers and response times.
findings.quote: so it's a queue with a faster timer.

findings.label: Missing proof
findings.finding: Build a written plan for what we do on on-sale morning.
findings.why: Halima asked to see it on paper, and Jordan had nothing, though he could have built one.
findings.quote: She wanted to see, on paper, what we do on an on-sale morning.

findings.label: Their words
findings.finding: Say 'a name, not a queue' instead of 'support plans'.
findings.why: Halima talked about who picks up when things break, and nobody said 'support'.
findings.quote: I don't buy uptime, I buy what happens when it's down.
